tasks.short: Lead the 13-person HR team: priorities, one-on-ones, escalations, checking work across recruitment, payroll, absence and ER cases.

today.trigger: Daily stand-ups, weekly one-on-ones, escalations from HRBPs, recruiters and payroll by Teams and mail.
steps: Scan Outlook and Teams for escalations and open cases
Hold one-on-ones and team meetings, assign work
Check status of vacancies in Recruitee, absence cases in AFAS and payroll close
Decide on difficult employee relations and labour relations cases
Report team progress to the management team
drudgery: Chasing status updates across three sites
Building weekly status overviews by hand
Re-reading long mail threads before a decision
today.time_sinks: Collecting status from people and systems before the real conversation starts; meetings that only exchange information.

lenses.faster: A Monday brief built from Recruitee, AFAS absence cases and the payroll calendar replaces status rounds; one-on-ones start from the facts.
lenses.autonomous: Alerts fire on events (a poortwachter deadline nearing, a vacancy stuck in a stage 14 days, a payroll check failing) instead of the director asking.
lenses.ambitious: Real coaching for every team member each month, with a development plan tied to the North Star, instead of firefighting.
lenses.joy: Less chasing and status gathering; more time for coaching and the hard cases people value the director for.
lenses.options: For a tricky case, get three handling options with CAO and legal points before deciding.
lenses.altitude: Design the team's operating rhythm and the dashboards and alerts that run it, rather than collecting status personally.
reach: Team-level reporting that the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst now builds by hand
First-pass case triage that HR Business Partners do today

tasks.human_edge: Trust, judgement on people and conflict, accountability for decisions about staff, and the relationship with the works council and site managers.
tasks.pattern_why: Leading people stays human; AI only prepares briefs, summaries and options.

in_practice.trigger: Every Monday 07:00 and on event alerts from AFAS and Recruitee.
steps: Pull open vacancies, stage ages and offers from Recruitee
Pull open absence cases and poortwachter deadlines from AFAS
Summarise escalated mail threads and Teams chats
Produce a one-page brief per team member and a team overview
Director uses it in one-on-ones and decides actions
in_practice.human_gate: Director decides all assignments and people decisions; the brief has no authority.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot summarises Outlook threads and Teams meetings.
Status briefs combining ATS and HRIS data cut preparation time for team leads.

risks: Team members feel monitored if briefs track individuals (works council consent under WOR art. 27 may apply)
Summaries miss nuance in sensitive cases
AVG: absence data in briefs must stay need-to-know
research_questions: How many hours per week does the director spend collecting status before decisions?
Does the AFAS and Recruitee API give the fields needed for a weekly brief without manual exports?
Would the works council see individual-level briefs as a personnel tracking system needing consent?

tasks.short: Answer managers' policy questions (harassment, equal treatment, CAO rules) and propose policy changes to the MT.

today.trigger: A manager calls, mails or meets the director with a policy question or an incident.
steps: Hear the question or incident from the manager
Look up the policy on SharePoint, the CAO text and the law
Give advice by phone or mail, sometimes after legal check
Note patterns and draft a policy change for the MT and works council
drudgery: Answering the same CAO and policy questions repeatedly
Searching policy documents and CAO articles
Rewriting advice mails for each manager
today.time_sinks: Repeat questions from site managers that a well-searched policy would answer; drafting change proposals from scratch.

lenses.faster: Managers get a cited answer from policy and CAO texts in minutes; the director handles only what is new or sensitive.
lenses.autonomous: A Teams policy assistant answers routine questions around the clock and routes harassment, discrimination and dismissal topics straight to HR.
lenses.ambitious: Every manager, including shift leads on all three sites, gets consistent advice, and question logs show which policies are unclear.
lenses.joy: No more answering the same leave or overtime question for the tenth time; time goes to real cases and better policies.
lenses.options: For a policy change, draft three variants with cost, legal risk and works council impact side by side.
lenses.altitude: Own the policy knowledge base and the assistant's answer quality, reviewing logs and fixing gaps.
reach: Routine policy questions now handled by HR Business Partners and HR Administrators
First drafts of policy texts that external counsel writes today

tasks.human_edge: Handling harassment and integrity cases with care and confidentiality, judging context, and carrying the advice with managers and the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: Routine answers can be retrieved and cited automatically; sensitive cases and any policy change need a person to approve.

in_practice.trigger: A manager asks a question in a Teams HR channel or mail.
steps: Assistant classifies the question; sensitive topics go straight to HR
Retrieve relevant policy, CAO article and legal source from SharePoint
Draft an answer with citations
Routine answers go out; flagged ones wait for HRBP or director approval
Monthly, cluster questions and draft policy change proposals
in_practice.human_gate: Director or HRBP approves flagged answers and every policy change before it goes to MT and works council.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list of questions, answers and approvals

evidence.claim: Copilot Studio can build a Teams agent grounded in SharePoint documents.
Policy Q&A bots reduce routine HR questions to the HR team.

risks: Wrong or outdated answer on CAO rules creates a claim
Harassment reports handled by a bot instead of a confidential adviser
Policies on SharePoint not current, so answers inherit errors
research_questions: What share of manager questions in the last three months were routine and answerable from existing documents?
Are both CAO texts and all policies current and in one SharePoint library?
What accuracy do managers and HRBPs measure on a test set of 50 real questions?

tasks.short: Dig into absence, turnover and hiring data to find causes of people problems and propose fixes.

today.trigger: Monthly MT report, a spike in verzuim or early leavers, or a question from the MT.
steps: Ask the People Analytics analyst for extracts from Power BI and AFAS
Combine with Recruitee and Studytube data in Excel
Look for patterns by site, shift, manager and contract type
Write findings and recommendations for the MT
drudgery: Joining exports in Excel
Cleaning inconsistent site and department codes
Rebuilding the same charts each month
today.time_sinks: Data preparation and back-and-forth with the analyst before any interpretation.

lenses.faster: A monthly pack links hires to 90-day retention, absence and training completion by site and shift, with draft explanations.
lenses.autonomous: Anomaly checks on the nightly AFAS extract flag a site or team whose absence or early leaving jumps.
lenses.ambitious: Track the North Star per vacancy and per manager, and test which onboarding steps actually predict day-90 retention.
lenses.joy: No more Excel joining; time goes to asking why and testing fixes with managers.
lenses.options: Several candidate explanations with the data that supports or weakens each, instead of one story.
lenses.altitude: Define the questions, metrics and checks; review the pack and decide which hypotheses get tested.
reach: Routine reporting by the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Workforce cost insight that FP&A asks HR for

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the sites and managers, judging which pattern is real, and turning findings into actions people accept.
tasks.pattern_why: Data joins are deterministic; explanation drafting is an LLM step; the director checks before anything reaches the MT.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh; monthly pack on day 5.
steps: Join AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube data on employee number in the Power BI model
Run fixed metrics and anomaly checks per site, shift and team
Draft narrative and possible causes with supporting figures
Director and analyst review, adjust and add recommendations
Publish to the MT
in_practice.human_gate: Director signs off findings and recommendations; no individual-level conclusions leave HR.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI workspace and SharePoint MT pack archive

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI drafts narrative summaries of report pages.
Automated anomaly detection on HR metrics is feasible on a nightly extract.

risks: Small teams make data identifiable (AVG); aggregate thresholds needed
Profiling employees may fall under EU AI Act high-risk use and needs works council consent
research_questions: Can AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube records be joined reliably on one key today?
Which three questions does the MT ask most that the current dashboard does not answer?
What minimum group size keeps reports anonymous enough for the works council and the AVG?

tasks.short: Plan and steer HR, training and labour relations activities across the three sites through the year.

today.trigger: Annual HR plan, quarterly reviews, CAO changes, works council meeting cycle.
steps: Draft the yearly HR plan with priorities and owners
Plan training calendar with L&D (mandatory certificates)
Prepare works council and union consultations
Track progress in quarterly reviews
drudgery: Compiling progress updates from owners
Making the same slides for MT and works council
Tracking certificate expiry overviews
today.time_sinks: Collecting progress and rewriting the plan into several audiences' formats.

lenses.faster: Plan, progress and works council papers come from one source; drafts for each audience are generated.
lenses.autonomous: Studytube certificate expiries (forklift, VCA, food safety) trigger enrolments and manager reminders without HR action.
lenses.ambitious: Plan workforce, training and labour relations as one plan linked to the North Star, refreshed quarterly instead of yearly.
lenses.joy: Less slide-making and chasing; more time with the works council and site leads.
lenses.options: Scenario plans for peak season vs. low season, or with and without a new site contract.
lenses.altitude: Set the planning framework and decision rules; the system keeps status and drafts.
reach: Training calendar planning by L&D Specialists
Works council paper drafting by HR Business Partners

tasks.human_edge: Setting priorities, negotiating with the works council and unions, and keeping site managers on board.
tasks.pattern_why: The director leads planning and consultation; AI drafts and tracks.

in_practice.trigger: Quarterly review and each works council meeting cycle.
steps: Pull progress from the plan tracker and Studytube
Draft quarterly update and works council paper
Director edits and decides priorities
Publish to MT and works council
in_practice.human_gate: Director approves every plan and every paper going to the works council.

evidence.claim: Copilot drafts PowerPoint and Word documents from source files.
LMS platforms send automatic certificate expiry reminders.

risks: Generated works council papers sound generic and damage trust
Automatic enrolments clash with shift rosters
research_questions: How many hours per quarter go into progress collection and slides?
Can Studytube trigger enrolments on expiry by API or rule today?
Does the works council accept AI-drafted papers if the director signs them?

tasks.short: Build and track the HR and personnel cost budget, including flex workers, CAO raises and training.

today.trigger: Annual budget round with Finance; monthly variance review.
steps: Export headcount and salaries from AFAS
Apply CAO increases, step raises and social charges in Excel
Add flex worker volumes and agency rates
Agree with Controller and FP&A, then track monthly variance
drudgery: Rebuilding the Excel model each year
Reconciling agency invoices to orders
Explaining variances line by line
today.time_sinks: Manual model assembly and reconciling flex hours from three agency portals.

lenses.faster: A standing budget model reads AFAS and agency data and applies CAO rules, so the round starts from a draft.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly variance report on personnel and flex cost lands in Power BI with explanations of the largest gaps.
lenses.ambitious: Monthly reforecast of people cost per site, linked to the hiring forecast and season.
lenses.joy: No more Excel rebuilding; focus moves to trade-offs with Finance.
lenses.options: Budget scenarios: CAO outcome low/high, flex share 15 vs 25 percent, absence at 5 vs 7 percent.
lenses.altitude: Own the model's assumptions and rules; FP&A and HRIS run it.
reach: Personnel cost modelling done by FP&A Analysts
Flex invoice checks by Bookkeepers

tasks.human_edge: Making trade-offs and defending the budget with the Finance Director and MT.
tasks.pattern_why: CAO scales, charges and rates are written rules on structured data; output can be checked.

in_practice.trigger: Budget kick-off in September; monthly close.
steps: Load AFAS headcount, scales and contracts
Apply CAO and social charge rules
Add flex volumes and rates from agency data
Produce scenarios and variance with short LLM-written comments
Director and Controller review and approve
in_practice.human_gate: Director and Controller approve the budget and each reforecast.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI finance workspace, budget versions in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Rule-based personnel cost models on HRIS data are common practice in FP&A.

risks: Rule errors in CAO raises spread to the whole budget
Agency data formats differ and break the load
research_questions: Do all three agency portals offer an export or API for hours and rates?
How far did last year's Excel budget miss actual personnel cost, and why?
Who in FP&A or HRIS would own the model?

tasks.short: Keep up with labour law, court rulings and CAO changes in transport and warehousing.

today.trigger: Newsletters, law firm updates, CAO negotiation news, new legislation.
steps: Read newsletters, sector updates and rulings
Check impact on Noordhaven's policies and CAO practice
Share relevant changes with HRBPs and MT
drudgery: Skimming many updates with little relevance
Rewriting summaries for colleagues
today.time_sinks: Reading volume; most items do not apply to Noordhaven.

lenses.faster: A weekly digest filters updates to those touching Noordhaven's CAOs, flex use and absence process, with impact notes.
lenses.autonomous: Runs weekly on set sources (rechtspraak.nl, overheid.nl, sector and union sites) without a prompt.
lenses.ambitious: An impact register per change, with owner and deadline, so nothing like a new flex worker rule is missed.
lenses.joy: Stop wading through newsletters; read five relevant items with context.
lenses.options: For a big change, scenarios of how it hits cost and processes.
lenses.altitude: Curate the sources and relevance rules; check the register.
reach: Legal update work of external counsel
Compliance briefings by HR Business Partners

tasks.human_edge: Judging what matters for this company and its labour relations, and when to call a lawyer.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured texts become a structured, citable digest inside a fixed weekly workflow.

steps: Collect new items from fixed sources
Classify relevance against Noordhaven profile (CAOs, flex, sites, verzuim)
Summarise with links and impact note
Director reviews and assigns follow-ups
in_practice.human_gate: Director decides what action follows; digest is input only.

evidence.claim: LLMs can summarise and classify legal updates with source links.

risks: Missed relevant item gives false confidence
research_questions: Which sources hold 90 percent of relevant items for this sector?
Does a three-month pilot catch everything counsel flagged in the same period?
Is the digest trusted enough to drop paid newsletters?

tasks.short: Oversee job descriptions and grading of positions under both CAO function systems.

today.trigger: New or changed role, reorganisation, employee objection to grading.
steps: Collect role information from manager
Write or update job description in Word
Grade against CAO function system with HR committee
Handle objections and register in AFAS
drudgery: Writing job descriptions from scratch
Comparing to reference functions by hand
today.time_sinks: Back and forth with managers on job content; consistency checks across sites.

lenses.faster: Draft description and proposed grade with reference function comparison in an hour.
lenses.autonomous: Changes in role content flagged from reorganisation plans for re-grading.
lenses.ambitious: A consistent function house across three sites, reviewed every year.
lenses.joy: Less writing; more talking with managers about what the job really is.
lenses.options: Several grading arguments, showing where a role sits between two levels.
lenses.altitude: Own the function house and grading rules; review proposals.
reach: Job description drafting by HRBPs
Grade checks by the Compensation and Benefits Specialist

tasks.human_edge: Fair grading, handling objections, and consultation with works council and unions.
tasks.pattern_why: Grading affects pay and is contested; AI drafts, people decide.

in_practice.trigger: Request for new or changed role.
steps: Manager fills structured role questionnaire
AI drafts description and compares to reference functions
Committee reviews and decides grade
Register in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Grading committee and director decide every grade.
data_needed: CAO function systems and reference functions

evidence.claim: LLMs draft job descriptions from structured input.

risks: Bias in grading proposals (EU pay transparency directive)
research_questions: How many grading cases per year and how long does each take?
Can the reference functions be shared with an AI tool under licence?
Does the works council accept AI-assisted proposals?

tasks.short: Forecast staff needs per site and season, including flex workers.

today.trigger: Annual budget, new customer contract, peak season planning.
steps: Get volume plans from operations
Estimate FTE per site with turnover and absence
Split permanent and flex
Share with MT and agencies
drudgery: Manual Excel forecasting
Re-doing it when volumes change
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the forecast each time operations change volumes.

lenses.faster: A forecast model recalculates in minutes when volumes change.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly refresh from AFAS turnover and absence data, alerting on gaps.
lenses.ambitious: Rolling twelve-month forecast per site and shift, shared with agencies early.
lenses.options: Scenarios for contracts won or lost, turnover high or low.
lenses.altitude: Own the assumptions and check outcomes.
reach: Workforce planning by FP&A
Flex ordering plans with agencies

tasks.human_edge: Judgement on business plans and choices between permanent and flex.
tasks.pattern_why: Drivers and rules are known; structured data; checkable.

steps: Load volumes and productivity norms
Apply turnover, absence and hiring lead time
Produce scenarios
Director reviews

evidence.claim: Driver-based workforce models are standard practice.

risks: Bad volume input gives bad forecast
research_questions: Are productivity norms per site documented?
How accurate were past forecasts?
Will operations share volume plans monthly?

role.altitude: From answering, compiling and forecasting by hand to designing and checking the HR system: data model, policy assistant, budget and forecast models, and the rules and gates around them.
reach: Routine reporting of the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Personnel cost and workforce modelling with FP&A
First-line policy questions of HR Business Partners
Legal update work now bought from external counsel
role.ceiling_note: About 30 to 40 percent of time can be freed; leadership, works council relations, conflict and people decisions stay human, and EU AI Act and AVG limits apply to employee data.
skills_to_grow: Defining metrics and data quality rules
Reviewing AI output and setting gates
EU AI Act and AVG for HR use
role.ambitious_version: Run HR on one data model that links every hire to day-90 outcome, with rolling forecasts, a policy assistant for all managers, and the director's time spent on site leaders and the works council.
